The Mid-Autumn Festival is a traditional East Asian holiday celebrated on the 15th day of the 8th month of the lunar calendar. The full moon is an important symbol of the festival because its round, complete shape represents wholeness, reunion, and togetherness. Mooncakes are traditionally shared with family and friends as a symbol of reunion and togetherness, making them a special part of the celebration. Students who celebrate the Mid-Autumn Festival are invited to join us for a mooncake-making gathering on Friday, September 25th at 3:30 PM in the South Church Kitchen. Questions? Please see Ms. Davis in Streeter 255.

Fellowship of Christian Athletes (FCA) is starting this Friday! FCA is a student group focused on faith, sports, and their impacts on our lives. Our conversations will be rooted in the Christian faith, but you don’t have to be a Christian or an athlete to come. We’ll meet Friday mornings from 7:00–7:40 on Court 3 in the Field House. FCA is student-led, and we’re looking for students who want to help lead and shape this group. Come check it out this Friday!

Our XC teams are hosting their one and only home meet on Tuesday. We were unable to host a meet last year, so we want our community to be conscious of runners on campus Tuesday afternoon beginning at 3:30 until approximately 5:00. At 3:15 tomorrow, the exits to South Main St and Barker Ave will be closed and remain so until the races are finished. During this time, you must exit via Brantview Dr. Please be aware that the course does cross Brantview Dr. to Stowe Green. Mr. Garcia will be there to manage traffic that is coming and going. Thank you for helping us deliver a safe and great race! Go Toppers!

On Thursday, October 1st the REAL Club will meet at Tinker House at 3pm to walk together down to St. Johnsbury School for a special presentation for teens on making smart choices. The presentation will be from 3:30-4:30 and will address vaping, anxiety & depression, social media, and bullying. Snacks and door prizes are available. For questions, reach out to Mrs. Sweet.

Scholars’ Bowl traveled to Essex on Saturday for the Sue Pasco Opening Tournament where the SJA A Team dominated and went undefeated. In their closest competition of the day, they won by 165 points. They won that match against the SJA B Team. Congratulations to all the Scholars: Amos Donn, Gaia Kennedy, Charlie Peralez, Jonah Raser, Raine Rashid, Alexey Strokanov, Poppy Shattuck, and Sophie White. Thanks to Chef Hale for guiding the team.

Boys Cross Country competed at the U-32 Invitational over the weekend. The JV team finished 2nd, just one point behind BFA St. Albans, led by Stone Thomas in 2nd overall. The Varsity team won the meet by eight points over U32, led by John Thornton Sherman in 3rd, Bryan Stocker in 4th, and Manny Fliegelman in 5th.

For Girls Cross Country, Willa Mantius set the tone for the Academy by securing a top 15 overall finish. The defining highlight of the team’s performance came from its middle pack, where Bailey Qualter and Elsie Kidder ran stride-for-stride through the chute, to seal two crucial scoring positions. The JV team’s charge was ignited by Bella Annello and Wenonah Brewer-Nyborg, who ran virtually shoulder-to-shoulder through the tape. Bella earned 16th place overall, while Wenonah chased her in just three seconds later for 17th overall. Sophomore Lyda Bentley delivered another season-best clocking to keep the Hilltoppers within striking distance, placing 23rd overall.

Of the roughly 700 people on our meal plan, 150 to 200 people come to lunch each day without their ID cards. That’s a lot of people, and it makes the job of our Food Services team more difficult. Please be sure to bring your ID card to lunch and have it ready when you get to the front of the line. Think of it as a small way to say thank you to the people who arrive hours before most of us and work all day to feed us. Having your ID ready is one easy way we can take care of them.

The Girls Varsity Tennis Team will be holding informal hit-arounds on Thursdays from 4:00 to 5:30 p.m. at the Kiwanis tennis courts, weather permitting. Can you spot the troll? Do you know what a troll is? Members of Mr. Eckhardt’s Contemporary Issues class have been studying Media Literacy, including misinformation and disinformation. As part of the class, they have created both ‘real’ and ‘troll’ social media accounts. They are posted on the first floor of Colby Hall. Can you tell the difference? Test your knowledge all this week.

If you frequent Ranger Breezeway, you may have seen the opening exhibit of the tiny art gallery that opened on campus last week. Tiny Art Gallery will strike again in October with two shows, the first in celebration of Indigenous People’s Day and the second in celebration of all things spooky. This is a call to all visual artists interested in our tiny project: create a tiny portrait, painting, watercolor, collage within one of these themes. A drop-box with instructions will launch Monday in Student Life. Submissions for the first theme are due Thursday, October 8. Submissions for the spooky theme are due Monday, October 19. You may also submit any questions to Tiny Art Gallery’s anonymous directors via this drop-box.
